theorem sourceIntervalCompletion_eq_image_of_interior (ν : Measure BridgeNoise)
    (a z S w : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hz : |z| ≤ a) (hS : 0 < S) (hw : |w| ≤ a)
    (hImage : ∀ U : ℝ, 0 < U → ∀ v : ℝ, |v| < a →
      intervalCompletion ν a v U z = intervalImageCandidate a z U v) :
    sourceIntervalCompletion ν a w S z = intervalImageCandidate a z S w := by
  by_cases hw' : |w| < a
  · rw [sourceIntervalCompletion_pos ν a w S z hS]
    exact hImage S hS w hw'
  · have hzero : sourceIntervalCompletion ν a w S z = 0 :=
      sourceIntervalCompletion_exterior ν a w S z (fun h => hw' h.1)
    rw [hzero]
    have heq : |w| = a := le_antisymm hw (le_of_not_gt hw')
    rcases le_total 0 w with hw0 | hw0
    · have hwA : w = a := by simpa only [abs_of_nonneg hw0] using heq
      rw [hwA]
      exact (intervalImageCandidate_upper_wall a z S ha hz hS).symm
    · have hneg : -w = a := by simpa only [abs_of_nonpos hw0] using heq
      have hwA : w = -a := by linarith only [hneg]
      rw [hwA]
      exact (intervalImageCandidate_lower_wall a z S ha hz hS).symm

theorem sourceIntervalCompletion_spatial_hasDerivAt_of_image (ν : Measure BridgeNoise)
    (a y T z : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hy : |y| < a) (hz : |z| ≤ a) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hImage : ∀ U : ℝ, 0 < U → ∀ v : ℝ, |v| < a →
      intervalCompletion ν a v U z = intervalImageCandidate a z U v) :
    HasDerivAt (fun w => sourceIntervalCompletion ν a w T z)
      (deriv (intervalImageCandidate a z T) y) y := by
  have hDiff : DifferentiableAt ℝ (intervalImageCandidate a z T) y :=
    (imageCandidateSpatial_hasDerivAt 0 a z T y ha hz hT hy).differentiableAt
  have heq : (fun w => sourceIntervalCompletion ν a w T z) =ᶠ[𝓝 y]
      intervalImageCandidate a z T := by
    filter_upwards [isOpen_Ioo.mem_nhds (abs_lt.mp hy)] with w hw
    rw [sourceIntervalCompletion_pos ν a w T z hT]
    exact hImage T hT w (abs_lt.mpr hw)
  exact hDiff.hasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq heq

theorem sourceRemainder_eq_image_of_interior (ν : Measure BridgeNoise)
    (a y T z b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hy : |y| < a) (hz : |z| ≤ a) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hsmall : b ^ 2 ≤ T / 2) (hnew : |y + b| ≤ a)
    (hImage : ∀ U : ℝ, 0 < U → ∀ v : ℝ, |v| < a →
      intervalCompletion ν a v U z = intervalImageCandidate a z U v) :
    sourceRemainder ν a y T z b =
      intervalImageCandidate a z (T - b ^ 2) (y + b) - intervalImageCandidate a z T y -
        (b - b ^ 2 * (z - y) / T) * deriv (intervalImageCandidate a z T) y := by
  have hS : 0 < T - b ^ 2 := by linarith only [hT, hsmall]
  unfold sourceRemainder
  rw [sourceIntervalCompletion_eq_image_of_interior ν a z (T - b ^ 2) (y + b) ha hz hS hnew hImage,
    sourceIntervalCompletion_eq_image_of_interior ν a z T y ha hz hT hy.le hImage,
    (sourceIntervalCompletion_spatial_hasDerivAt_of_image ν a y T z ha hy hz hT hImage).deriv]

theorem sourceRemainder_small_bound_of_image (ν : Measure BridgeNoise)
    (a y T z b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hy : |y| < a) (hz : |z| ≤ a) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hsmall : b ^ 2 ≤ T / 2) (hnew : |y + b| ≤ a)
    (hImage : ∀ U : ℝ, 0 < U → ∀ v : ℝ, |v| < a →
      intervalCompletion ν a v U z = intervalImageCandidate a z U v) :
    |sourceRemainder ν a y T z b| ≤
      compensatedProfileConstant * (|b| / Real.sqrt T) ^ 3 *
        (1 + |z - y| / Real.sqrt T) ^ 3 * intervalIncrementProfile a y T z b := by
  rw [sourceRemainder_eq_image_of_interior ν a y T z b ha hy hz hT hsmall hnew hImage]
  exact intervalImageCandidate_compensated_small_step_closed_bound a y z T b ha hy hz hT hsmall hnew

theorem actual_interval_retained_bound_of_image
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (hB : IsBrownianReal B P)
    (a y T z b : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hy : |y| < a) (hz : |z| < a) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hb : b ^ 2 ≤ T) (hzero : T - b ^ 2 = 0 → y + b = z)
    (hImage : ∀ U : ℝ, 0 < U → ∀ v : ℝ, |v| < a →
      intervalCompletion (bridgeLaw B P) a v U z = intervalImageCandidate a z U v) :
    |retainedRemainder (bridgeLaw B P) a y T z b| + negativeOvershoot (bridgeLaw B P) a y T z b ≤
      (2 * compensatedProfileConstant + 40) * (|b| / Real.sqrt T) ^ 3 *
        (1 + |z - y| / Real.sqrt T) ^ 3 * intervalEnvelope a y T z b := by
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (bridgeLaw B P) := isProbabilityMeasure_bridgeLaw B P hB
  have hRegular := (sourceIntervalCompletion_spatial_hasDerivAt_of_image
    (bridgeLaw B P) a y T z ha hy hz.le hT hImage).differentiableAt
  apply actual_interval_local_gaussian_bound (bridgeLaw B P) a y T z b compensatedProfileConstant
    ha hy hz hT hb compensatedProfileConstant_nonneg hzero hRegular
  · intro S hS w hw
    exact Shao.C2.BridgeUpperAffineIdentification.bridge_upper_formula B P hB a w S z hS hw (abs_lt.mp hz).2
  · intro S hS w hw
    exact Shao.C2.BridgeLowerIdentification.bridge_lower_formula B P hB a w S z hS hw (abs_lt.mp hz).1
  · intro β hβ hnew
    have hbound := sourceRemainder_small_bound_of_image (bridgeLaw B P) a y T z β
      ha hy hz.le hT hβ hnew hImage
    convert hbound using 1 <;> ring

end Shao.C2.BridgeIntervalImageConsumer

\subsection{A common completion kernel and its local remainders}

For a fixed $a>0$ let $I$ be either $(-a,a)$, $(-\infty,a)$, or
$(-a,\infty)$. For interior endpoints $y,z$ and $T>0$, define
\begin{equation}\label{cn:kerneldef}
 f^I_a(y,T;z)=\frac{k_T^I(y,z)}{\phi_T(z-y)},\qquad
 \phi_T(d)=(2\pi T)^{-1/2}e^{-d^2/(2T)}.
\end{equation}
This is the strict Brownian-bridge survival probability. We suppress $a,I$
when fixed. Its extension is zero if either endpoint is on or outside
the monitored walls. At a reachable zero-energy future its two endpoints
coincide; its value is one if that endpoint is interior. For terminal
envelopes only, a zero-variance bridge with different endpoints means
their deterministic linear interpolation. For $a=0$ all completions
are assigned zero.

Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of monitored wall signs: $\{+1,-1\}$ for
the interval, $\{+1\}$ for the upper half-line, and $\{-1\}$ for the
lower half-line. Write
\[
 d=z-y,\quad D=1+|d|/\sqrt T,\quad
 u_\eta=a-\eta y,\quad v_\eta=a-\eta z,
\]
\begin{equation}\label{cn:profiles}
 P(y,T;z)=\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal S}e^{-u_\eta v_\eta/T},
 \qquad
 P_b(y,T;z)=\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal S}
 e^{-(u_\eta-|b|)_+v_\eta/T}.
\end{equation}
In particular every such profile is at most two. Differentiation always
holds the walls and terminal endpoint fixed.

\begin{lemma}[Derivative and Taylor bounds]\label{cn:kernel}
For fixed nonnegative integers $j,l$, in particular for $j+l\le3$,
\begin{equation}\label{cn:derivative}
 |\partial_y^j\partial_T^l(f-1)|
 \le C_{j,l}T^{-j/2-l}D^jP(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
The same one-sided estimates hold at a wall. The quotient satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{cn:PDE}
 f_T=\tfrac12f_{yy}+(d/T)f_y.
\end{equation}
For $b^2\le T$, define the compensated remainder at an actual reveal by
\begin{equation}\label{cn:remainder}
 \mathfrak r_b=f_{\mathrm{ext}}(y+b,T-b^2;z)-f(y,T;z)
                 -(b-b^2d/T)f_y(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
If $b^2\le T/2$ and the new spatial point is in the closed domain,
\begin{equation}\label{cn:smallTaylor}
 |\mathfrak r_b|
 \le C|b|^3T^{-3/2}D^3P_b(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For a half-line, $f=1-e^{-2u_\eta v_\eta/T}$ by reflection. For
$\eta=+1$, put $C=2(a-y)(a-z)$; the reflected case is identical.
The exponent is affine in $y$, and
$|C_y|\le2|d|+\sqrt{2C}$. Repeated differentiation gives a polynomial
in $C/T$, times $C_y^jT^{-j-l}e^{-C/T}$. Absorbing the polynomial
and the powers of $\sqrt{C/T}$ into half the exponential proves
\eqref{cn:derivative}, with no lower bound on either endpoint.

For the interval, the image expansion divided by the free density is
\begin{align*}
 f&=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(e^{-A_m/T}-e^{-B_m/T}),\\
 A_m&=8m^2a^2+4ma d,\qquad
 B_m=2(y+(2m+1)a)(z+(2m+1)a).
\end{align*}
Here $A_0=0$ supplies the constant one; every other exponent is
nonnegative and affine in $y$. Each such exponent $C$ satisfies
$|C_y|\le2|d|+\sqrt{2C}$: for $A_m$ use
$A_m=(A_{m,y}-d)^2/2-d^2/2$, and for $B_m$ use that its two factors
have the same sign and differ by $d$. Thus a differentiated image term
is bounded by
\[
 C_{j,l}T^{-j/2-l}D^j e^{-C/(2T)}.
\]
When $T\le a^2$, set $B_0=2u_-v_-$ and $B_{-1}=2u_+v_+$.
For $m\ge1$,
\[
 B_m\ge B_0+8m^2a^2,\qquad
 A_m\ge B_0+8m(m-1)a^2.
\]
The second inequality follows from
$A_1-B_0=2(a-y)(3a+z)\ge0$ and $d\ge-2a$.
The negative side similarly has
$A_{-m}\ge B_{-1}+8m(m-1)a^2$, using
$A_{-1}-B_{-1}=2(a+y)(3a-z)\ge0$, and the analogous square tail
for the remaining $B$ terms. Their Gaussian series is bounded by a
constant times $P$. This proves \eqref{cn:derivative} in this range.

If $T\ge a^2$, the sine expansion of the killed heat kernel yields
\[
 |\partial_y^j\partial_T^l k_T^I|
 \le C_{j,l}T^{-(j+2l+1)/2}.
\]
For example, after taking absolute values its series is bounded by
$Ca^{-j-2l-1}\sum_{m\ge1}m^{j+2l}e^{-c m^2T/a^2}$;
the exponential dominates the required power for $T/a^2\ge1$.
Since $|d|/\sqrt T\le2$, derivatives of the reciprocal free density
have the corresponding bounds
$CT^{(1-j-2l)/2}$. Leibniz's rule bounds every positive-order
derivative of $f$ by $CT^{-j/2-l}$. For order zero use
$|f-1|\le1$. Finally $u_\eta v_\eta\le4a^2\le4T$, so
$P\ge2e^{-4}$. This proves the desired profile estimate also here.
The normally convergent positive-time expansions justify all
differentiations and one-sided traces. Dividing the heat equation for
$k$ by the free heat equation gives \eqref{cn:PDE}.

For \eqref{cn:smallTaylor}, apply second-order Taylor expansion along
$(y+sb,T-sb^2)$, $0\le s\le1$. Its variance time is in $[T/2,T]$,
its drift factor is at most $CD$, and its profile is at most $P_b$.
The leading terms are
\[
 b f_y-b^2 f_T+\tfrac12b^2f_{yy}
 =(b-b^2d/T)f_y.
\]
The other second-order terms are $-b^3f_{yT}+b^4f_{TT}/2$.
Each third-order directional term has normalized power
$(|b|/\sqrt T)^{j+2l}D^j$ with $j+l=3$. Since
$|b|/\sqrt T\le1$ and $j+2l\ge3$, all these terms are at most
$C|b|^3T^{-3/2}D^3P_b$. A point on the wall uses the smooth
one-sided zero trace.

\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A projection pays its own negative overshoot]\label{cn:projection}
Suppose $y,z\in I$ and $y+b$ hits or crosses a monitored wall with
sign $\eta=\operatorname{sign}(b)$, where $b^2\le T/2$. Put
\[
 B=|b|,\quad u=a-\eta y\in(0,B],\quad p=\eta u,\quad
 \delta=B-u,\quad c=1-\eta(B+u)d/T.
\]
Then, for the interval and either half-line,
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak r_b&=\mathfrak r_p+O_b,
 &O_b&=-\eta\delta c f_y,\qquad0\le c\le2D,
                                                        \label{cn:projectionid}\\
 |\mathfrak r_p|+(O_b)_-
 &\le CuB^2T^{-3/2}D^3
 \le CB^3T^{-3/2}D^3.                                  \label{cn:projectbound}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Both the crossing and its projection have zero completion, so
subtraction in \eqref{cn:remainder} proves the identity. Since
$\eta d<u$, one has
$c\ge1-2b^2/T\ge0$ and
$c\le1+2(B/\sqrt T)(D-1)\le2D$.
The projected segment has time at least $T/2$; thus
\eqref{cn:smallTaylor}, with $|p|=u$ and $P_p\le2$, gives
$|\mathfrak r_p|\le Cu^3T^{-3/2}D^3$.

Set $A=1-\eta ud/T\ge1-u^2/T\ge1/2$. Nonnegativity of $f$ and the exact identity
$\mathfrak r_p=-f-\eta uAf_y$ imply
$uA(\eta f_y)_+\le|\mathfrak r_p|$.
The identity $((B+u)/u)A-c=B/u$ gives $c/A\le(B+u)/u$, so
\[
 |\mathfrak r_p|+(O_b)_-
 \le\left(1+\frac{\delta(B+u)}{u^2}\right)|\mathfrak r_p|
 \le C\{u^3+\delta u(B+u)\}T^{-3/2}D^3
 =CuB^2T^{-3/2}D^3.
\]
The projected displacement need not be a remaining label. Equality
hits have $\delta=0$; the projected endpoint uses the one-sided wall trace.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One local Gaussian wall envelope]\label{cn:localprofile}
At any actual reveal state with $a,T>0$, $y,z\in I$ and $b^2\le T$,
let $\ell_b^I$ retain $\mathfrak r_b$ except at a small-energy crossing,
where it retains $\mathfrak r_p$. For each monitored wall put
\[
 w_\eta=a-\eta y,\quad M_\eta=|b|+(\eta d)_+,\quad
 \Pi=\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal S}e^{-((w_\eta-M_\eta)_+)^2/T},
 \qquad q=|b|/\sqrt T.
\]
Then, with the second term present only for an interval,
\begin{equation}\label{cn:localprofilebound}
 |\ell_b^I|+1_{\{\text{small-energy crossing}\}}(O_b)_-
 \le Cq^3D^3\Pi.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a small interior step use \eqref{cn:smallTaylor} and the wallwise
inequality
$(w_\eta-|b|)_+(w_\eta-\eta d)
\ge((w_\eta-M_\eta)_+)^2$, which gives $P_b\le\Pi$.
For a large interior step, $|f'-f|\le(1-f)+(1-f')$; each reflection
deficit is bounded by the sum of $e^{-2uv/T'}$ over monitored walls.
If $w_\eta>M_\eta$, all their endpoint distances from that wall
are at least $w_\eta-M_\eta$, and the future variance is at most $T$;
otherwise that wall's summand of $\Pi$ is one. Thus the deficits
cost $C\Pi$. By \eqref{cn:derivative}, the compensation is at most
$C(q+q^2|d|/\sqrt T)DP\le CqD^2\Pi$.
Here $q\le1$, and $q>1/\sqrt2$ lets $q^3$ pay both one and $q$.
At any crossing its crossed wall has $0<w_\eta\le|b|\le M_\eta$,
so $\Pi\ge1$: use \eqref{cn:projectbound} for a small crossing. At a large crossing its future completion is
zero, so $|f'-f|\le1$; the same compensation bound proves the claim.
Equality hits are crossings, and a reachable zero-time interior future
has deficit zero. No separated positive overshoot is included.
\end{proof}



\subsection{A common exponential estimate for both moment budgets}

$k_T^J(y,z)$ be the Brownian transition density killed on leaving
$J$, and put
\[
 f_a^J(y,T;z)=\frac{k_T^J(y,z)}{\phi_T(z-y)},\qquad
 \phi_T(u)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi T}}e^{-u^2/(2T)}.
\]
This is the survival probability of the bridge from $y$ to $z$ in
variance time $T$. It is zero at an exterior endpoint. We denote the
upper and lower half-line completions by $f_a^+$ and $f_a^-$.
All three completions use the same raw endpoint and the same remaining
square sum. For $T>0$, their backward equation is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bridgepde_main}
 f_T=\tfrac12 f_{yy}+\frac{z-y}{T}f_y.
\end{equation}
With $d=z-y$, write $D=1+|d|/\sqrt T$ for $T>0$. For a next
increment $b$, subtract the leading term from the actual update to define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bridge_remainder_main}
 \mathfrak r_b^J=f_{a,\mathrm{ext}}^J(y+b,T-b^2;z)
       -f_a^J(y,T;z)-(b-b^2d/T)(f_a^J)_y(y,T;z).
\end{equation}
The extension retains a crossing as a killed state, including equality.
The factor $b-b^2d/T$ follows from \eqref{eq:bridgepde_main}; replacing
the remaining square sum by a deterministic variance would change it.


Let $A_r^J$ be strict survival of the revealed path in $J$ through rank $r$.
For exterior endpoints and $Q=0$ every completion is zero. At zero
remaining energy use the reachable terminal value, as specified with
\textup{(S.8.11)}. For the compact assembly put
$h=4n\sigma^2R^2$ and $\kappa=\inf\{0\le r\le n:Q-Q_r<h\}$.
\subsection{Exact cancellation after a permutation reveal}
\begin{lemma}[Conditional permutation compensation]\label{cn:telescope}
For any $x>0$ and deterministic $H>0$, put
$\kappa_H=\inf\{r:Q-Q_r<H\}$ and let $\nu\le\kappa_H$ be
a bounded stopping rank in the following reveal filtration. Condition
on the full raw labeled sample and reveal an independent uniform
permutation of its labels. Put $V_r^J=1_{A_r^J}f_a^J(S_r,Q-Q_r;S_n)$
for each monitored domain $J$, zero on exterior terminal endpoints
or $Q=0$, with the stated reachable $T=0$ convention. Then
\begin{equation}\label{cn:telescopeid}
 EV_\nu^J-EV_0^J
 =E\sum_{r<\nu}1_{A_r^J}1_{\{S_n\in J\}}
                         \mathfrak r_{X_{r+1}}.
\end{equation}
The expectation includes the sample and its independent permutation.
If $m$ is any measurable permutation-invariant function of the whole
sample with $|m|\le1$, the same identity holds after multiplication
of both sides and every summand by $m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The conditioned population, its full $Q$, its endpoint $S_n$, and
its wall $a$ are all known at time zero. At a reveal state, the sum
and square sum of the $t=n-r$ remaining labels are exactly $d,T$.
Their uniform average satisfies
\[
 \frac1t\sum_{b\ \mathrm{remaining}}(b-b^2d/T)=0.
\]
For $r<\nu$, $T\ge H>0$. The conditional mean of the next
increment in $V_r^J$ is consequently the conditional mean of the
compensated remainder, times the live and endpoint indicators.
Both the cutoff event and these indicators are measurable in the
current conditioned reveal filtration. Finite stopped telescoping
gives \eqref{cn:telescopeid}.

There is no missing integrability condition: every actual population
satisfies $|b|\le\sqrt T$ and $|d|\le\sqrt{tT}$. The first
derivative bound therefore gives
$|\mathfrak r_b|\le C(1+t)$, since
\[
 |b-b^2d/T||f_y|
 \le C\left(\frac{|b|}{\sqrt T}
            +\frac{b^2|d|}{T^{3/2}}\right)D
 \le CD^2\le C(1+t).
\]
Projected terms and separated overshoots have the same finite bound.
There are only finitely many ranks. Dead and exterior-endpoint states
are identically zero and require no derivative evaluation.

The unconditioned reordered sequence again has the original iid
ordered law, so all estimates proved at deterministic original iid
ranks apply after averaging. Finally $m$ is fixed under the
conditioned permutation reveal, which proves the masked identity.
No stopping-time assertion for the original natural iid filtration
has been made.
\end{proof}
